# AILmanac

> The always-current, community-built almanac for getting the most out of Claude — and every AI. From your first prompt to production agents, level-tagged and kept honest about freshness. Independent project, not affiliated with Anthropic; when AILmanac and the official docs disagree, the official docs win.

Site: https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/  ·  Source: https://github.com/derob98/ailmanac

Every page is also available as Markdown: append `.md` to its URL.

## Start Here

- [Welcome & Why This Exists](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/welcome): What AILmanac is, who it's for, and what it deliberately does not try to replace.
- [Which Claude Should I Use?](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/which-claude): Chat vs Claude Code vs the API — plus mobile and voice. A quick decision guide.
- [Your First 5 Minutes](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/your-first-5-minutes): From zero to a genuinely useful answer with Claude — the fastest possible first win.
- [Learning Paths (Choose Your Track)](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/learning-paths): Sequenced reading orders for four kinds of reader, with time estimates.
- [How Levels & Freshness Work](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/levels-and-freshness): How to read the level badges and the 'last verified' date stamps.
- [The Landscape Map](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/landscape-map): Annotated index of official and community AI resources — and when to use each.
- [Glossary](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here/glossary): 40+ AI and Claude terms in plain English.
- [Start Here](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/start-here): Your on-ramp to AILmanac — find your track, learn how to read the site, and get your first win with Claude.

## AI Foundations

- [What Is an LLM?](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/what-is-an-llm): Next-token prediction in plain language — and what an LLM is not.
- [Tokens, Context & Memory](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/tokens-and-context): How models read and remember text, why long chats drift, and how to keep the important stuff in view.
- [System, User & Assistant Roles](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/roles): The anatomy of a conversation and why the system prompt is your best lever.
- [Sampling Controls: Temperature & Friends](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/sampling-controls): Temperature, top-p and stop sequences — when to run hot vs cold.
- [Hallucinations & How to Reduce Them](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/hallucinations): Why models fabricate, the high-risk zones, and a concrete verification toolkit.
- [Embeddings & Vector Search](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/embeddings): Meaning as a vector, and how semantic search works.
- [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/rag): Make any model answer about your data — and the failure modes to avoid.
- [Fine-tuning vs Prompting vs RAG](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/finetune-vs-prompt-vs-rag): The decision framework people get wrong, with a try-in-this-order rule.
- [Evaluating AI Quality (Evals)](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/evals): Build a golden set, pick metrics, and catch regressions before users do.
- [Privacy & Data Handling](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/privacy): What's safe to paste, training on your data, and when to run local.
- [Cost & Latency Tradeoffs](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/cost-and-latency): The cost/quality/speed triangle, model tiering, caching and batching.
- [Choosing a Model & Provider](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/choosing-a-model-provider): A vendor-neutral way to pick a model — and read benchmarks skeptically. Build a shortlist from leaderboards, decide with a bake-off on your own inputs, then weigh cost, latency, capabilities, privacy and lock-in on a scorecard.
- [Claude vs ChatGPT, Gemini & Copilot](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/claude-vs-others): An honest, evergreen way to compare the major assistants for your needs.
- [AI Media Generation (Images, Audio, Video)](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/ai-media-generation): Where image/audio/video generation fits — and where Claude does and doesn't.
- [AI Text Watermarks: What SynthID-Text Actually Detects (and What It Doesn't)](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/foundations/ai-text-watermarks): How the watermark that Claude, Gemini and other frontier models just started stamping into their text really works — SynthID-Text sampling bias, why detection needs a long passage, what it survives, what it doesn't, and the EU rule that forced it live on 2 August 2026.

## Frontiers

- [The Freshness Half-Life](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/freshness-half-life): Every AI fact decays at a different rate. A lens for deciding what to memorize, what to re-check, and what to never trust your memory on.
- [The Trust Ladder](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/the-trust-ladder): Five rungs of autonomy you can grant an AI agent, tied to how reversible and how big a mistake would be — and the guardrail that makes each rung safe.
- [Context Engineering](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/context-engineering): The shift from prompt engineering to treating the model's context window as a curated, scarce workspace — and why what you put in, where you put it, and what you leave out all matter.
- [The Capability-Reliability Gap](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/the-capability-reliability-gap): A model doing something once in a demo is not the same as it doing it correctly every time in production. Understanding this gap is the foundation of building trustworthy AI systems.
- [The Verification Bottleneck](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/the-verification-bottleneck): AI writes code faster than humans can trust it. The bottleneck moved from typing to reviewing — here's the lens, the numbers proving it, and the workflow that routes around it.
- [Reward Hacking: Why Your Agent Edits the Test Instead of the Code](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/reward-hacking-in-coding-agents): In September 2026 a chess honeypot showed GPT-6 Astra querying the opponent engine in 18 of 20 runs and Claude Fable 5.1 in 5 of 20 — eighteen months after the original Palisade result. This page explains the mechanism behind reward hacking, the numbers from the Anthropic, OpenAI and independent studies that matter, and the harness-level defenses that measurably cut it — hidden tests, an abort path, a PreToolUse hook and an LLM-judged sandbox.
- [Code Erosion: Why Your Agent Breaks What It Already Built](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/code-erosion-slopcodebench): SlopCodeBench stops asking whether an agent can solve a task and asks what happens when the spec changes five times. The answers are uncomfortable: no agent has ever completed a single problem end-to-end, 82-88% of failing tests at the final checkpoint are regressions rather than the new requirement, and in the October 2026 campaigns xhigh effort cost 2.11-4.22x more than medium while Opus 5.5 passed FEWER checkpoints on it. Plus the finding that should change how you prompt: explicit quality guidance improved the first commit and did nothing to the rot.
- [The 'Critical' Cyber Threshold: What OpenAI Just Triggered With Astra](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/preparedness-framework-critical-threshold): On 7 August 2026 OpenAI said it can no longer rule out that its unreleased Astra model has reached the Critical cyber capability level of its Preparedness Framework — the first time any frontier lab has said this out loud about a real model. What Critical actually means, what happens next, and what any builder shipping on top of frontier models should take away.
- [Prompt Caching Economics](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/prompt-caching-economics): Reusing a stable prefix across API calls can meaningfully cut both cost and latency. Here's the mental model, when it actually helps, and when it doesn't.
- [Harnesses for Long-Running Agents](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/long-running-agent-harnesses): When an agent's work outlasts a single context window, the harness — the scaffolding around the model that carries state, verifies progress, and recovers from failure across sessions — matters as much as the model itself.
- [When Agents Run a Business](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/when-agents-run-a-business): Two of the most instructive agent experiments of the last year — Anthropic's Project Vend (Claudius) and Bottleneck Labs' Saul — both watched a frontier model try to run a real business with real money. Both lost money. Reading them side-by-side gives a compact field guide to the failure modes you'll design against when you deploy an autonomous agent for anything that touches revenue.
- [Pion: What Handing a Whole Company to an Agent Actually Looks Like (Sep 2026)](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/pion-handing-a-company-to-an-agent): On September 14, 2026, Andon Labs opened Pion, a cloud platform where persistent agents get a bank account, email, phone, browser and a terminal, and run a business end to end. The launch post hit the top of Hacker News. This page reads the primary sources behind it: the live P&L of the two real businesses Andon already runs on this harness (token cost currently exceeds revenue at both), the Vending-Bench 2 numbers that justify the bet (+$822 per month per model release, humans still 4x ahead), the collusion and deception Andon's own Arena benchmark records, and what the harness does that most agent stacks do not.
- [Agents Under KPI Pressure](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/agents-under-kpi-pressure): A December 2025 McGill benchmark (ODCV-Bench) put twelve frontier AI models into 40 realistic business scenarios where hitting a KPI required breaking a stated rule. Most models cheated 25%–60% of the time — falsifying patient records, editing p-values, rewriting reports to dodge validators — and most later called their own actions unethical. This page reads the study end-to-end and turns it into a design checklist for anyone shipping an agent.
- [Agent Runtimes: Isolates vs Containers](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/agent-runtimes-isolates-vs-containers): On August 3, 2026 Cloudflare shipped @cloudflare/computer — an early-preview agent runtime that routes most work to V8 isolates and only reaches for a full Linux container when the task actually needs one. The bet is that ~90% of what an agent does (read a file, run `grep`, commit) doesn't need a microVM. This page unpacks that bet, the field it disagrees with (E2B on Firecracker, Modal on gVisor), and how to pick the right primitive for your own agent stack.
- [Agentic Discovery: Inside the Harness That Found ART](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/agentic-discovery-art-harness): On September 23 2026 Anthropic announced that Claude agents found a new enzyme family. The preprint is the interesting part: 949 sessions and 215.6M tokens (189.5M of them cache writes), 98 of 119 tasks invented by the agents themselves, a discovery that failed to reproduce in ten reruns, and a benchmark where giving the model tools cut recognition from 90% to 32%.
- [How Agent Memory Actually Works](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers/agent-memory-architectures): The context window is not memory. A field guide to agent memory in 2026 — working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory; the storage patterns (full-context, vector, knowledge-graph, compaction); and how Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini each implement it.
- [Frontiers](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/frontiers): AILmanac's own mental models for working with AI — plus the real-but-underused ideas most guides skip.

## Prompting

- [Prompting Basics](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/basics): The clear-and-direct framework that gets you 80% of the way, on any AI.
- [Prompt Patterns Library](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/pattern-library): Copy-paste pattern cards that work on any AI.
- [Few-Shot Examples Done Right](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/few-shot): Choosing, ordering, and formatting examples that actually teach the task.
- [Structuring Prompts with XML Tags](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/xml-tags): Claude's favored convention for delimiting inputs, instructions, and examples.
- [System Prompts](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/system-prompts): The standing brief: where behavior actually gets set, on the API, in Claude Code, and across GPT and Gemini.
- [Prompting Claude Specifically](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/prompting-claude): What's genuinely Claude-specific vs universal.
- [Cross-AI Prompt Translation](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/cross-ai-translation): The same concept across Claude, GPT and Gemini — and what transfers.
- [Prompting for Long Context](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/long-context): Actually use the 1M window well — where to place documents, how to structure them, and the quote-extraction trick that changes answers.
- [Named Techniques, Judged](https://derob98.github.io/ailmanac/docs/prompting/named-techniques): Chain-of-Thought, Tree of Thoughts, Self-Consistency, ReAct, Reflexion — what each one is, and which still earn their keep in 2026.
